reden: Yes. The audit explicitly reports that TimelockTokenPool.withdraw(address,bytes) signs only a static message without nonce/contract/chain binding, making signatures replayable. It explains that anyone can call withdraw(_to, sig) repeatedly (and even across pools), withdrawing additional unlocked tokens over time—exactly the same root cause and attack path as the described issue. The same fix (adding nonce/replay protection and proper domain binding) would resolve both.
